en.headline: Privacy watchdog arrests 29-year-old man over alleged doxxing after boxing match
en.dek: The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data said the Chinese national was detained in Kowloon today and granted bail pending further investigation.
body: The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data arrested a 29-year-old Chinese national in Kowloon on Thursday on suspicion of disclosing personal data without the data subject’s consent, contrary to section 64(3A) of the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance.

Investigators said the man had targeted the victim after both took part in the same boxing match in early 2025. Posts allegedly appeared on two social-media accounts in March 2025 and August 2026 that disclosed the victim’s English name, Chinese alias, social-media handles, the social-media account of his employer and photographs, together with negative comments.

The arrested man was granted bail. The Privacy Commissioner’s Office said it would continue the investigation and reminded the public that doxxing is a serious offence carrying a maximum penalty of a HK$1 million fine and five years’ imprisonment.

zh.headline: 私隱專員公署拘29歲男 涉拳賽後「起底」對手
zh.dek: 公署今日在九龍區拘捕一名中國籍男子，涉嫌未經同意披露個人資料，已准保釋繼續調查。
body: 個人資料私隱專員公署今日在九龍區拘捕一名29歲中國籍男子，他涉嫌在未經資料當事人同意下披露個人資料，違反《個人資料（私隱）條例》第64(3A)條。
調查顯示，被捕男子自2025年年初與事主參加同一場拳擊比賽後開始針對對方。2025年3月及2026年8月，有人先後在兩個社交媒體平台帳戶發布帖文，披露事主的英文姓名、中文別名、社交平台帳戶名稱、現職公司社交平台帳戶名稱及照片，並作出負面評論。
被捕人士已獲准保釋，私隱專員公署會繼續調查。公署提醒市民，不要因私人糾紛將他人「起底」；「起底」屬嚴重罪行，一經定罪最高可處罰款100萬元及監禁5年。
